caption: The drawing depicts the interior of a print shop filled with various printing equipment and tools. In the foreground, there are two large printing presses—one on the left with a lever and a plate spotted with black ink, and another on the right featuring rotating wheels and gears. Both presses are black and metallic. Scattered on the floor and surfaces near the presses are sheets of white paper and other printing materials. Several stools with reddish-brown round seats and black or blue legs are positioned near the workstations. In the center background, there is a wooden shelving unit or type case holding compartments for type blocks, with more type trays visible further back against the right wall. Hanging from the ceiling above the work area is a large green and brass lamp. The walls are painted shades of pink, purple, and beige, and the floorboards are green. Posters, notes, and schedules are pinned to the walls throughout the workspace. A black pipe runs across the room near the ceiling, and a sign with the words “The Tyrant’s Foe, The People’s Friend, Pacific Press” hangs from the pipe. On the right wall, a clock and a fan are mounted, and another closed wooden cabinet appears along the left side. The ceiling features large windows or skylights letting in natural light, and several more books and paper stacks are distributed around the printing room.
title: Print Shop, 1870
